build.stencil: Stencilled: each frame is sprayed onto its tower through a cut sheet, a little crooked every time.
build.poster: Billposted: every frame is pasted up beside its tower in rows, sheet over sheet.
build.spray: Tagged: the route from source to cut is sprayed across the city and left to fade.
build.none: Carried by hand, one frame a bar, and set into its floor.
build.phosphor: Drawn in light: every route from source to film is left glowing, so the city fills with the paths the cuts took.
build.set: Broadcast: the frame is not carried. It jumps in three channel changes and arrives.
build.silhouette: Hung on a rod, like a shadow puppet, and walked across.
build.cave: Carried as heat: the floor it reaches stays hot long after.
build.embers: Burned in: the frame lights its floor and goes up as an ember.
build.circle: Wound in: the carrier spirals round its path on the way, as a needle would.
build.sun: Burned onto the eye: each delivery leaves an afterimage of the whole city.
build.card: Printed: every delivered frame is laid beside its tower in rows, a contact sheet of the cut.
build.bay: Measured: each frame travels with its in time, its out time and its length.
build.paper: Pasted: each frame is stuck to its tower at whatever angle it landed.
build.worms: Trailed: the frame leaves copies of itself along the way, so the route is a strip of film.
build.ink: Run in: the route from source to cut is left as a line of dye across the city, and fades as dye does.
build.wash: Bled in: the frame lights its floor, then lifts off and thins out like ink in water.
build.watercolour: Washed in: each frame is laid on its tower wet, at whatever angle it settled.
build.sumi: Brushed: the route from source to cut is one stroke of ink across the city.
build.impasto: Laid on: frames are set beside the tower in rows, like dabs on a palette.
build.woodblock: Pulled: frames are printed in rows beside the tower, an edition of the cut.
build.cyanotype: Exposed: each frame is laid on its tower and left in the light.
build.riso: Run off: frames are stacked beside the tower in rows, sheet after sheet.
build.xray: Traced: the route from source to cut is a line of light through the glass.

looks.name: DEEP WATER
looks.rule: Every animal squeezes when its sound plays.
looks.test: With the swerve off, can you still pick it out? If so, the lateness is not what you were seeing.

looks.name: WARM PHOSPHOR
looks.after: Afterlight 14: long-exposure light painting. Only the lights survive, and every kick turns the exposure
looks.rule: Light fades. Every trail is gone in about a second.
looks.test: Does the cleared frame on the downbeat feel like a new section? Off, the downbeat has to do that alone.

looks.name: THE SET
looks.after: Afterlight 13 and 19: a 1950s television. Every cut changes the channel; the picture is scanned in lines
looks.rule: Every cut changes the channel, and every channel shows the orchestra.
looks.test: Do you read the empty channel as a mistake, or as the film underneath? Off, there is no way to ask.

looks.name: SILHOUETTE THEATRE
looks.after: Afterlight 02 and 26: cut-outs against lit tissue, with one red
looks.rule: Red belongs to whoever is sounding brightest.
looks.test: Can you hear its sound by watching the red go out?

looks.name: WARM CAVE
looks.after: Afterlight 08: what the skin knows. Everything is seen as heat
looks.rule: Sound is heat. Whatever plays runs hot.
looks.test: Without the ring, would you have found it? If not, heat is carrying the timing, not the squeeze.

looks.name: LIGHT ALONE
looks.after: Afterlight 11: only light. The film is embers rising in wind
looks.rule: Embers rise.
looks.test: Does the bass now look heavy? Off, it is only large.

looks.name: MAGIC CIRCLE
looks.after: Afterlight 16: the film wound into a turning record under the orchestra; each beat sends a ripple out
looks.rule: The corps circles the record one way.
looks.test: Do the passes fall on beats? They are not made to. If they seem to, you supplied that.

looks.name: SUN IN YOUR EYES
looks.after: Afterlight 20: the eye keeps a complementary afterimage at every cut, and every kick is a blink
looks.rule: The eye keeps an afterimage at every cut.
looks.test: Did you believe the picture changed? Off, every afterimage is honest.

looks.name: THE CARD
looks.after: Afterlight 26: the frame engraved, hatched by its own light
looks.rule: More light is more ink. Everything that plays is engraved.
looks.test: Can you tell where it is from how the others make room?

looks.name: THE MEASURED BAY
looks.after: The Crash-Test Family: a measured bay, where every stroke is scored
looks.rule: In the bay everything is on time and on the grid.
looks.test: Off, find the latest animal yourself. Then turn it on and see if you were right.

looks.name: CUT PAPER
looks.after: Small Sun and WYGWYL: flat cut paper, a few colours
looks.rule: Four sheets of paper. Brightness chooses the sheet.
looks.test: Is the red a drum? Mute nothing, look away, and count kicks by the flashes.

looks.name: SPACETIME WORMS
looks.after: Afterlight 17: whatever moves leaves a body of light back through time
looks.rule: Whatever moves leaves a body of light behind it.
looks.test: Does the still one look dead, or like the only one keeping time?

looks.name: THE LIBRARY
looks.own: a new world: a reading room after hours
looks.rule: In the library everyone whispers: every stroke is small and dim.
looks.test: Does it read as rude, or as the soloist? In STRAIGHT, is anyone the soloist?

looks.name: THE DATA CENTER
looks.own: a new world: a cold aisle between racks
looks.rule: Every sound lights the racks of its own lane.
looks.test: Do you begin to hear a part that is not there?

looks.name: STENCIL
looks.own: the street: two cut sheets and a can, on a rolled cream ground
looks.rule: Two sheets only: black for whatever is lit, red for whatever is brightest.
looks.test: With two colours, can you still tell who is playing? If not, the stencil is too coarse for music.

looks.name: CUT POSTER
looks.own: the street: three flat colours, red on top, pasted to a wall
looks.rule: Three flat colours. Nothing is shaded; things are one colour or the next.
looks.test: Does a poster that moves stay a poster, or become a cartoon?

looks.name: SPRAY WALL
looks.own: the street: the orchestra sprayed on concrete in its own colours
looks.rule: Everything lit is sprayed, with mist round it, and the heavy marks run.
looks.test: Is the still one the tag you would remember tomorrow?

looks.name: INK ON FILM
looks.own: paint: dye on clear film, in bands that run along the strip and step frame by frame
looks.rule: Each animal leaves dye where it has been. The dye is pulled along the film, and each narrow band of film slips every few frames, which steps the edges.

looks.name: WET INK
looks.own: paint: ink still wet and out of focus, pulled along the film
looks.rule: Nothing has an edge. Every animal is a bloom of its own colour, and blooms that meet make a third colour.

looks.name: WATERCOLOUR
looks.own: paint: a pencil drawing, then washes on cold-pressed paper
looks.rule: Pencil first, then water. A wash is strongest at its edge, where the pigment is left when it dries.

looks.name: INK WASH
looks.own: paint: black ink in three dilutions on fibrous paper, and one red seal
looks.rule: One colour, three dilutions. Loud is black, quiet is grey, and where the brush runs dry the paper shows.

looks.name: THICK PAINT
looks.own: paint: loaded brush dabs laid along the way things move
looks.rule: Every mark is one dab of thick paint, laid in the direction things are moving.

looks.name: WOODBLOCK
looks.own: print: indigo, slate and rust blocks on cream, with the grain of the wood
looks.rule: Four blocks: indigo for the dark, slate for the half-lit, bare paper for the lit, rust for the brightest. Every flat carries the grain.

looks.name: CYANOTYPE
looks.own: print: Prussian blue paper, white where the thing lay
looks.rule: Whatever lies on the paper stays white. The longer it stays, the whiter.

looks.name: RISOGRAPH
looks.own: print: pink, yellow and blue drums and black, out of register, in a grain of dots
looks.rule: Three drums and black, each a little out of register. Warm things print pink and yellow, cool things blue.

looks.name: GLASS
looks.own: print: everything is glass; only edges and thickness show
looks.rule: Everything is glass. You see edges, and thickness, and whatever is behind.

looks.name: THE VIDEO STORE
looks.own: a new world: a rental store, long closed and half flooded
looks.rule: Every tape on the shelves is a real Bolas film with a frame of itself on the cover. The televisions play the one taken down. Touch a tape to rent it.
looks.test: Which screen do you end up watching?

looks.name: THE FILM DEPOT
looks.own: a new world: an archive aisle of film cans, with one reel running at the far end
looks.rule: Every can is a film nobody is watching. One is running on the screen at the end of the aisle: a real file. Touch to change the reel.

looks.name: THE WET COLLECTION
looks.own: a new world: a museum store of specimens in jars
looks.rule: Every jar holds one that stayed. The orchestra is the ones that are still moving.

looks.name: THE ORBIT
looks.own: a new world: an observation deck above a planet, with film strung between masts
looks.rule: Up here nothing falls. The film is strung out in the open and the orchestra drifts between the ribbons.

looks.name: CRASH LAB
looks.own: a celluloid city · a library of stacks
looks.rule: 26 Bolas films stand here as towers built of their own frames.
looks.test: What would this city need to have kept for a film to be rebuilt here?

looks.name: OUT OF LIFE
looks.own: a celluloid city · an underwater data center
looks.rule: This city keeps 1,546 shots from 121 films: a tower for each film, a floor for each shot. On every street the jellies go into the towers, looking.
looks.test: Before it gets there: which floor do you think it is going to? In STRAIGHT they all come back empty, and no film is made.
